reason: Legal on every hard rule and it is the one chapter the spec forbids inventing a venue for (R9: 'the plate is a street of those seven premises'). Venue type named first, place_category 'village shop row' is three lowercase words and matches the place text, anchor is inanimate and cuts lower-left to upper-right, and the activity ('taking in the morning delivery') is a real verb 18 people can each be seen performing at their own doorway. All seven required SCENE_TOKENs get an explicit, architecturally-scaled hosting line — colliery gates, weaving workshop, police box, five-storey hotel, club side door with the horseshoe magnet, dairy, mynah over the seed merchant — and the delivery round supplies release/reuptake as native trade action rather than metaphor, which is the R5 requirement met without invention. 'MESSENGER ROW' is 2 words, reads as an ordinary street nameplate and does not print the topic word. Two conditions on the redraw: (a) the pit gate must stay a closing element at the head of the road, not the subject, or the plate starts reading as ch4's mine; (b) 7 tokens + 16 stock props is at the top of the density budget at 1376x768 — cap required lettered strings at 8 per §9.

The hosting of the chapter's single most important token is physically incoherent. `place` says 'lock-up stalls down both sides' of 'one long central aisle', and the anchor is that aisle; but stock_props and hosts_tokens then put 'a rug stall with a loom running the length of the central aisle' with 'the loom set on the floor seam'. A loom occupying the full length of the aisle contradicts the stall layout, blocks the declared activity (shoppers 'working down the aisle with a basket'), and breaks the one-perspective/physically-coherent rule. Secondary: structurally this is ch3 again in the same batch — a run of small trading units, one per token, with the RAPHE weaving unit on the midline and a postal-delivery reuptake worker. ch3 is spec-mandated, so ch5 is the one that has to differentiate. The acronym itself ('5 HIGH TOWN' = 5-H-T as word initials) and the TAROT_2A hosting (curtained booth with the pie stall = 2C, wash-down channels = 3, book stall = 6 opening off it) are genuinely good and worth keeping.
better_alternative: Keep the covered market hall, rebuild the layout as a real market-hall CENTRAL ISLAND: one long narrow island lock-up on the hall's midline is the raphe rug workshop (it literally sits on the seam and ships rolled rugs out to every counter in the building), with a walking aisle down each side and the perimeter runs on both outer walls. Anchor becomes 'the central island run and its floor seam, corner to corner'; the shopping activity is then unobstructed and the raphe's ship-everywhere geometry is stronger, not weaker. Push the tarot booth, the all-night kiosk and the bus-stop booth to the corner arches as now, and move the postman to the island's own delivery end so SERT collects from the seam. Differentiate from ch3 by trade register: ch3 is the delivery-in morning, ch5 is the customer's mid-morning shop.

reason: A travelling circus is a spectacle venue, and three separate failures follow from having picked it to hold three tokens at once rather than for the pun. (1) The declared activity is 'putting the tent up', but BEETHOVEN_ORCHESTRA is hosted as a seated band on a rostrum with drums, brass and winds and a conductor on the box — a full band cannot be raising canvas, so the token and the one-shared-activity rule (R4) contradict each other. (2) ALPHA_WOLF_PACK is placed loose on open ground 'between the trees and the horse lines'. Loose wolves beside a picketed horse line is not a physically coherent showground; a circus wolf act travels in a cage wagon. (3) A blue police box is street furniture on a town pavement; it does not stand at the gate of a field a travelling show pitched in last night, so LOCUS_COERULEUS_BLUEPOST is bolted on. Also near-duplicates the existing county-fair midway world (ch89) and the promenade amusement family. 'NOR'EAST' as the NOR- morpheme plus the fixed N-compass is the one part that works.
better_alternative: A municipal park bandstand on a frosty Sunday — place_category 'park bandstand'. Every token becomes native instead of imported: the bandstand rostrum IS Beethoven's stand (heart-drums one side, brass and winds the other, the fishing NET hung on the stand's stair by the park keeper); a blue police box stands at the park gates, which is exactly where police boxes stood; and the park's snowy pine belt runs behind the railings with the numbered-collar pack out on the frosted grass beyond the deer fence and the keeper's dart rifle in the fence hut — a fenced enclosure inside a Victorian park, which is not the zoo category. Anchor: the bandstand's raked steps and the iron park railing cutting the frame on a diagonal. Activity: everyone is turning out for the band concert — carrying and setting the folding chairs in rows, tuning, taking a seat, passing the collection tin. Sign 'NOR'EAST PARK BAND' (3 words). Mundane, unique, and the tent-raising/band contradiction disappears.

reason: The required SCENE_TOKEN cannot be hosted at a readable scale. DOPA_MINE is a course-wide fixed structure with four labelled pathway chambers, coal carts, the red D2 barrier, the up-elevators, the EXTRA pyramid hats and the DAT figure gathering ore back; this venue compresses all of it into one glass-cased penny-in-the-slot automaton against a side wall. In a 1376x768 frame carrying 22+ elements that cabinet is roughly a tenth of the frame width, so the four labelled chambers are unreadable — and §9 names resolution as the binding constraint that must be decided, not noted. Worse, it demotes a fixed course-wide structure to a miniature ornament: R9's rule is that a venue which cannot host the token is rejected, not the token. Secondary: an indoor seafront coin-amusement hall sits very close to the surviving promenade prize-shooting gallery (ch101) — same trade family, same furniture (shutter front, prize shelf above head height, coin counter, kick rail, queue for the next go). The fascia ('Hyper' as one morpheme, a name real arcades trade under) and the criteria carriers (minimum-token notice, accompanied-under-twelves door notice, branch board for the second setting, ticket tallies for the rating scales) are the strongest part and should be carried across.
better_alternative: Move ADHD onto the pit road so the mine can stand at architectural scale, exactly as ch3 does, and declare adjacent_to [4]: a coal merchant's bagging yard and weighbridge at the foot of the colliery road — place_category 'coal merchant's yard'. Activity: everyone is making up the round — shovelling and weighing a bag on the platform scale, stitching the neck, swinging it onto the lorry, and taking the weigh-ticket. The colliery gates and winding gear close the head of the yard full size with the four labelled gallery mouths in the gate yard. The criteria then ride on carriers whose real job is to bear them, keeping every device from the arcade version: the weigh-ticket spike = rating scales, the round board listing two delivery rounds = symptoms in two settings, the six-bag standard load chalked on the board = the symptom threshold, the date stamp on the ticket = age-of-onset before 12, and the minimum-load notice on the office window = the impairment threshold. Sign 'HYPERDRIVE HAULAGE' or 'HYPER FUELS'.

reason: Near-duplicate of two surviving venues, and the duplication is at the level of activity and props, not just category. ch43 (OCEAN DAILY CATCH, wet fish shop) is already 'pulling a numbered ticket, pointing at the row, weighing on the hanging dial, wrapping in paper' over a chilled slab with a hose and a numbered ticket queue; ch31 (MAYO'S AGED DELI) is already 'taking a ticket, waiting, pointing at the case, being handed wrapped parcels' over a long glass counter. This butcher is the third instance of the identical world — glass counter of cold cuts, take-a-ticket queue, hanging scale, wrapping-paper spindle, sawdust floor, price board. That is the six-launderettes failure the global dedup rule exists to stop: the chapter name will not retrieve a single unique world. Secondary: hosts_tokens is empty although communication_disorders and DSM_neurodevelopmental are required, and the four subtypes are asserted in the pun_explanation rather than given hosting lines. The fascia itself is excellent — keep 'tongue' on the sign.
better_alternative: TONGUE & GROOVE — a flooring and joinery mill, place_category 'joinery mill'. Tongue-and-groove is a genuine trade term and a name real joiners trade under, so the organ of articulation is still lettered on the fascia inside a trade with nothing to do with speech, and the world is unique across the 144. Activity: everyone is matching boards — feeding a board through the moulder, offering the tongue into the next board's groove, tapping it home, and stacking the run. All four subtypes then become native shop-floor business instead of restated clinical vignettes: boards whose tongue will not enter the groove at all = language disorder; boards machined to the wrong profile so the joint sits proud = speech sound disorder; the moulder that judders and repeats the same cut on one board = stuttering; and the mill's own posted feed-order rule (one man feeds, one man takes off, wait your turn at the outfeed) with the worker who keeps grabbing out of turn = social-pragmatic. The mirror move survives as the setting-out mirror over the outfeed table.

reason: Near-duplicate of #38 in this same batch. Both are trade-counter supply premises and their declared anchors are literally the same object: a floor-to-roof steel racking run of boxed trade stock crossing lower-left to upper-right, splitting the room into counter / test bench / stock wall / doorway. Both have a sign-out book on the counter (docket pad vs issue book), a bench where stock is triggered or sounded to prove it works, stock hanging on wall hooks, dated inspection labels on every item (test-and-tag expiry vs dated service tags) and graded sizes on a pegboard or size chart. Two chapters studied days apart would retrieve the same room. Of the pair this is the one that must move, because its strength is the phonetic pun and the pun is trade-independent: rent-a-X works on any hire business, whereas #38's one-hazard-per-bay isomorphism only exists in that specific shop. Secondary: the hand payoff is real but 'staff wiping their hands on rags' is weak literal depiction for a hallmark movement.
better_alternative: Keep RETT-A-... and move it to a marquee and event-hire yard, sign RETT-A-TENT HIRE. Activity: everyone erecting, striking and folding canvas. Rett then pays out harder than in a tool depot and with no counter-and-racking grammar: staff wringing out wet canvas by hand all shift is the hallmark hand-wringing as ordinary paid work, not a symbol of it; returned poles and winch handles come back with their grips stripped off, so purposeful hand use is what the yard has lost; nested ring-and-pole sets stacked in ascending diameters with the top three sizes missing is a native size chart carrying head-circumference deceleration. Prader-Willi comes off the catering-hire side (padlocked cold store, chained urn trolley, counted crockery). 22q11 still rides the damage-waiver and excess small print of the hire contract, which is CATCH-22 by its own name.

reason: Duplicates #28 inside the same batch, in a chapter it declares itself adjacent to, at both the anchor and the device level. Both venues are 'sunken vats set in a bench or floor, an overhead rail or pole above them, immerse the object, hang it to set, immerse it again' with the same lower-left-to-upper-right diagonal; and in both the repeat-dip is the mnemonic that carries chronicity (recurrence in 28, persistence in 32). Two adjacent plates sharing the anchor grammar AND the core device retrieve each other, which is the exact failure the global dedup rule exists to prevent. The name is fine and was already accepted; the trade is the problem.
better_alternative: Keep THYME & AGAIN (it says time and again, which is the chapter's whole point) and put it on a diary, calendar and almanac printing-and-binding works. Every carrier is then a printed duration in the trade's own units and there is not a vat in the building: tear-off day blocks for PDD's 'more days than not'; week-to-view spreads for the three-or-more outbursts a week; an almanac's printed lunar month with the final week shaded, which is PMDD's luteal week with no metaphor and no corpus-luteum detour; a two-year desk planner standing beside a school-year diary for the 2-year adult versus 1-year youth threshold. Activity: everyone collating, folding, stitching and guillotining date blocks. Anchor: the long collating table and the stitching-and-trimming run. Inter-episode mood and outbursts stay literal depiction at the folding bench.

reason: The world collides with a fixed lexicon entry and with three existing venues. DSM_bipolar's canonical prop in lexicon.json is 'a see-saw ... North-pole iceberg in the background (Lithium connection)', so ice and frost are already the course's signal for lithium; ch35, this venue's own declared neighbour, is Lithium Lift, a snow resort; ch6 and ch109 are both ice rinks. Making the entire Bipolar I plate a frozen white world makes the iceberg cue unretrievable (R7 triple collision across unrelated keys) and makes the 33-to-35 adjacency, which is supposed to encode drug-to-disorder, read as one continuous cold world in which the resident cannot say which building was the disorder. The freeze-tank versus thaw-tank device is genuinely good and worth keeping; the premises are not. Note also that this is the batch's third venue built on immersing objects in sunken tanks under overhead lifting gear (see 28 and 32).
better_alternative: Keep POLAR and move to an auto-electrical and battery shop, sign POLAR BATTERIES. Every item on the shelf literally has two poles stamped + and -, which is what bipolar means and is why the sign only has to spell half of it. The load tester's needle swings between two extremes on one unit; flat versus gassing-and-overcharged are the trade's own words for the two poles of the same battery; a charger faceplate carries a cycle counter as ordinary machine lettering, so rapid cycling appears verbatim on a dial whose native unit is cycles rather than metres; days on charge goes on the chalked bench tally; the trickle or maintenance charger on the bench is maintenance treatment; and ch35's lithium cells sit as a sibling boxed brand on the wall instead of swallowing the whole world.
